Interface Atom<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of value held by this atom
All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultAtom
public interface Atom<T>
A distributed AtomicReference with TTL-based leases and change notification.

An Atom is a keyed, shared reference whose value can be read, written, and watched by multiple processes. Every atom carries a time-to-live (TTL) lease; when the lease expires the atom is considered dead and further mutations throw AtomExpiredException. Callers can extend the lease with touch(Duration).

Subscriptions use coalescing semantics: subscribers always see the current state of the atom, not a replay of every intermediate value. If the atom changes multiple times between polls, the subscriber receives only the latest Snapshot. This is safe for use from multiple threads.

Usage examples

Blocking pattern: 

Atom<Session> sessionAtom =
    atomFactory.create("session:abc", Session.class, session, Duration.ofHours(1));

// Read current state
Snapshot<Session> current = sessionAtom.get();

// Watch for changes (blocking style)
BlockingSubscription<Snapshot<Session>> sub = sessionAtom.subscribe(current);
while (sub.isActive()) {
    switch (sub.next(Duration.ofSeconds(30))) {
        case NextResult.Value<Snapshot<Session>>(var snap) -> process(snap);
        case NextResult.Timeout<Snapshot<Session>> t -> { }
        case NextResult.Expired<Snapshot<Session>> e -> handleExpired();
        case NextResult.Deleted<Snapshot<Session>> d -> handleDeleted();
        default -> { }
    }
}

Callback pattern: 

Subscription sub = atom.subscribe(snap ->
    System.out.println("New value: " + snap.value()));
// later...
sub.cancel();

  • Method Details

    • set

      void set(T data, Duration ttl)
      Sets the value of this atom and resets its TTL.
      Parameters:
      data - the new value to store
      ttl - the new time-to-live for this atom
      Throws:
      AtomExpiredException - if the atom's lease has already elapsed or it has been deleted
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration

    • compareAndSet

      boolean compareAndSet(Snapshot<T> expected, T data, Duration ttl)
      Atomically sets the value of this atom only if its current token matches the one carried by expected. On success the TTL is reset and subscribers are notified; on failure nothing is written and no notification is sent.

      A false return is retryable — another writer won the race, so re-read and try again. AtomExpiredException is terminal — the atom is gone and retrying cannot succeed. 

      Snapshot<Session> current = atom.get();
Session next = current.value().withCount(current.value().count() + 1);
while (!atom.compareAndSet(current, next, Duration.ofHours(1))) {
  current = atom.get();
  next = current.value().withCount(current.value().count() + 1);
}
      Parameters:
      expected - the snapshot this write is conditioned on
      data - the new value to store
      ttl - the new time-to-live for this atom
      Returns:
      true if the write was committed, false if another writer changed the atom first
      Throws:
      AtomExpiredException - if the atom's lease has already elapsed or it has been deleted
      NullPointerException - if expected is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration

    • touch

      boolean touch(Duration ttl)
      Extends the TTL of this atom without changing its value.
      Parameters:
      ttl - the new time-to-live to apply
      Returns:
      true if the lease was successfully extended, false if the atom is already dead (expired or deleted)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is zero or negative, or exceeds the maximum allowed duration

    • get

      Snapshot<T> get()
      Returns the current value and staleness token of this atom.

      This is a synchronous, non-blocking read.

      Returns:
      a Snapshot containing the current value and its associated token
      Throws:
      AtomExpiredException - if the atom's lease has already elapsed or it has been deleted

    • delete

      void delete()
      Explicitly deletes this atom, immediately expiring its lease.

      After deletion, subsequent calls to set(T, Duration), get(), and touch(Duration) will behave as though the atom's TTL has elapsed.

    • subscribe

      BlockingSubscription<Snapshot<T>> subscribe()
      Subscribes from the current state using a blocking pull model. The first next() call returns the current snapshot (if the atom exists); subsequent next() calls block until the next set(T, Duration) occurs.
      Returns:
      a BlockingSubscription that yields Snapshot instances

    • subscribe

      BlockingSubscription<Snapshot<T>> subscribe(Snapshot<T> lastSeen)
      Subscribes from a known baseline using a blocking pull model. If the atom's current token differs from lastSeen.token(), the first next() call returns the current snapshot immediately; otherwise the first next() blocks until the next change.
      Parameters:
      lastSeen - the baseline to compare against, or null for equivalent behavior to subscribe()
      Returns:
      a BlockingSubscription that yields Snapshot instances

    • subscribe

      Subscription subscribe(Subscriber<Snapshot<T>> subscriber)
      Subscribes from the current state using a callback push model with a ready-made Subscriber.
      Parameters:
      subscriber - the subscriber to receive snapshot deliveries and lifecycle events
      Returns:
      a Subscription that can be used to cancel the subscription
